sources.label: US Mobile Light user on Warp in Uzbekistan: intermittent ordinary SMS, Wi-Fi call failure and overseas eSIM switch friction

events.outcome: Light remains USD 10 monthly or USD 96/year. Native roaming cannot work until the line has domestic U.S. usage; Warp/Dark Star Wi-Fi Calling setup also requires U.S. coverage.

events.scope: one first-person Warp/Verizon Light-plan user in Uzbekistan; Wi-Fi and handset details unknown; no named bank/app OTP
events.outcome: The original Light Plan user reports Wi-Fi calls failing, ordinary SMS briefly sending and receiving before stopping, and a failed attempt to install an eSIM after switching from Warp to Light Speed while already in Uzbekistan. In the same original thread, a US Mobile representative suggests weak Wi-Fi and advises arranging Wi-Fi Calling/network provisioning before departure; no successful resolution is shown. One January 2025 account, not a general activation ban, universal SMS failure or any named-app OTP result.

data.acquisitionSummary: Light is currently USD 10/month or USD 96 for 12 months, with 2 GB and unlimited domestic talk/text.

keep.action: Use the annual Light subscription for a current USD 96/year service path. No PAYG retention route or post-lapse number-hold interval is established here.

data.chinaActivation: eSIM delivery alone does not establish a complete overseas-first route. Native roaming requires prior domestic U.S. usage.
data.payment: Foreign-card acceptance is not treated as verified in this review.
data.wifiCalling: Included on Light. Warp and Dark Star setup requires U.S. coverage; Light Speed has a dashboard enablement flow.
data.roamingSms: Native roaming requires prior domestic U.S. usage; Light-specific China roaming/SMS availability is unresolved.
data.holdReason: USD 96/year is current, but native roaming requires prior domestic U.S. usage and some network choices require U.S.-side Wi-Fi Calling setup. China-first use is not established.
data.tariffSummary: Light: USD 10 monthly or USD 96/year; native roaming requires prior domestic U.S. usage.
guideSteps: Treat this as a U.S.-first route, not a China-first route.
If relying on roaming, establish domestic U.S. usage before departure.
Configure Wi-Fi Calling before departure when the selected network requires U.S. coverage for setup.
